verdict.line: You lose if you let her land a clean W (Ki Burst) into Q (Broken Wings) chain before level 3; you win if you out-sustain her cooldowns with E (Footwork) and Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks.

brief.thesis: Riven's entire kit is cooldown-gated — Q (Broken Wings) on 13s, W (Ki Burst) on 11-7s, E (Valor) on 10-6s — while K'Sante's E (Footwork) shield and Q (Ntofo Strikes) stack loop let him absorb and reset faster than she can re-threaten. That's why lane and solo-kill advantage both sit with K'Sante across 1,679 games, even though the overall 46.7% win rate shows the matchup reopens once her R (Blade of the Exile) hits rank 3 at level 16 and gives her a 10s-cooldown Wind Slash to duel with again.

theirWindow.what: She can chain W (Ki Burst) stun into Q (Broken Wings)'s triple reactivation for a real burst before your W (Path Maker) is even rank 2. Play passive, don't trade without E (Footwork) shield up.

yourWindow.what: Without E she has no damage block and no gap-close/escape. Proc Q (Ntofo Strikes) to 2 stacks for the shockwave pull, then land W (Path Maker)'s knockback-stun to lock the trade.

start.why: The most-picked start in these games (86.4% pick, 57.9% WR over 19 games) — the extra health and potion sustain let you absorb her early W-Q burst without losing the wave.

boots.why: 90% pick rate here — her passive Runic Blade empowers autoattacks, and her all-in strings lean on repeated hits, so flat physical reduction blunts exactly that pattern.

core.why: CDR shortens your Q (Ntofo Strikes) loop back to its 3.5s floor faster, and the proc slow keeps her inside Q range instead of resetting with E (Valor).
Damage reduction and health let you tank through her cooldown-limited all-in windows without losing the follow-up trade.
Stacking resistances scale your tankiness into the 13-18 window where her R (Blade of the Exile) rank 3 starts threatening duels again.

situational.when: the game goes long and you need a steady tool against her auto-reliant R (Blade of the Exile) phase
she's building lifesteal or crit and snowballing off kills
your team wants to group for fights off your All Out engages

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained health growth off autos during extended trades directly counters a matchup where she can't threaten you every cooldown — you out-heal her burst windows.

summoners.why: The dominant page here (90.9% pick, 50% WR) — Flash guarantees your W (Path Maker) or R (All Out) engage lands, and Teleport lets you reset and still make the all-in window her cooldowns open up.

playing.title: Hold E shield for her all-in
playing.detail: Don't trade into her W (Ki Burst) stun chain without E (Footwork)'s shield active — her Q (Broken Wings) reactivation hits three times in that stun.

playing.title: Build Q stacks before committing
playing.detail: Land two Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits to trigger the shockwave pull, which drags her into W (Path Maker) range for the stun-knockback follow-up.

playing.title: Punish her E cooldown
playing.detail: Her Valor cooldown runs 10/9/8/7/6s — once it's down she has no damage block or dash, so that's your window to initiate.

playing.title: Charge W through her burst
playing.detail: Path Maker's charge-up phase reduces damage taken before the dash fires — start it as she commits her combo, not after.

playing.title: Save R for her split-push threat
playing.detail: All Out (120s at rank 1) knocks her through walls and removes her escape options — use it to end lane rather than as a poke tool.

playing.title: Rush Iceborn's CDR loop
playing.detail: Faster Q resets mean more slow uptime, which denies her the dash resets she needs off Q (Broken Wings) and E (Valor).

playing.title: Respect her rank-3 R past level 16
playing.detail: Blade of the Exile's cooldown drops to 10s at rank 3, giving her a repeatable Wind Slash threat — stop free-trading and start playing around minion wave state instead.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, and summoner picks above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch; the trade-window and cooldown reasoning is our own analysis layered on top of the live ability text, not sourced from OP.GG.
